title: Novena for the Healing of the Sick
kicker: 9 days of hope in Christ who heals
card: For a friend or loved one who is ill: 9 days asking for healing, strength for caregivers and peace in God’s will.
ogDescription: 9 days of prayer for the healing of the sick, through Our Lady of Lourdes, St. Raphael, St. Camillus and St. Bernadette.
description: A 9-day Catholic novena for the healing of the sick, through Our Lady of Lourdes, St. Raphael, St. Camillus de Lellis and St. Bernadette.

epigraph.text: But for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings.

closingVerse.text: Beloved, I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in health; I know that it is well with your soul.

saints.name: St. Raphael
saints.bio: Archangel of the Book of Tobit, one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the saints. His name means “God heals”; he guided young Tobias and brought healing to Tobit’s eyes.
saints.alt: Painting: the Archangel Raphael, by Giovanni Biliverti

saints.name: St. Camillus de Lellis
saints.patron: Patron of the sick, nurses & hospitals
saints.bio: Soldier and gambler, converted in 1575, who gave his life to the sick. Though a leg wound troubled him for the rest of his life, he founded the Camillians, the Ministers of the Sick.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Camillus de Lellis wearing the red cross of his order, by Cristóbal Lozano

saints.name: St. Bernadette
saints.bio: Miller’s daughter to whom Our Lady appeared at Lourdes in 1858. As a Sister of Charity at Nevers she bore long illness with patience, and died at 35.

openingPrayer: Heavenly Father, You know the illness that N. is carrying: the pain and weariness of body and spirit, and the worry of all who love them. We bring this suffering to You, the Lord who heals, and we trust in Your loving care more than in our fear. Bless all who tend the sick. Today we ask St. Raphael, messenger of Your healing; St. Camillus de Lellis, servant of the sick; and St. Bernadette, patient in suffering, to join their prayers with ours before Your throne, through Christ our Lord.
closingPrayer: Lord Jesus, Divine Physician, lay Your healing hand on N. and on all the sick. Guide those who care for them, give us strength and peace, and let Your holy will be done.

tips.p: One person leads each part; all respond pray for us and Amen, and say the closing prayers together. The prayers say “we”; if you pray alone, say “I”.

If you can, go to Confession and attend Mass during these 9 days. Ask a priest about the Anointing of the Sick, which is for anyone seriously ill or facing major surgery, not only the dying. Pair prayer with good care: follow medical advice, offer practical help (Day 6), and be wary of anyone who promises a sure cure. At “N.”, say the sick person’s name; if you are praying for yourself, say “me”.

intentionPlaceholder: Write the name of the person you are praying for and the healing you ask.

days.title: Bringing Our Fear to Jesus
days.verse: So the sisters sent to him, saying, “Lord, he whom you love is ill.”
days.refl: Martha and Mary did not send Jesus a plan or a demand. They sent Him the plain truth: the one You love is ill. We can begin there too. Illness frightens us: the waiting for results, the pain we cannot take away, the questions no one can answer yet. We do not need to hide that fear or dress it up. We simply bring the one we love to Jesus, who loves them even more than we do.
days.more: Fear in the face of illness is not a failure of faith. Grieving for His friend Lazarus, Jesus Himself wept (John 11:35). He does not ask us to pretend to be strong. St. Bernadette knew sickness from childhood: she survived cholera as a girl and lived with asthma for the rest of her life. Like her, we can bring our weakness to God honestly, and let Him meet us there.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, You know N. by name, and You know how heavy this illness is for them and for all of us who love them. We are afraid, and we tell You so. With Martha and Mary, we bring N. to Jesus with simple trust. Through the prayers of St. Bernadette, calm our fears, comfort N. in body and spirit, and help us take each day as it comes.
days.step: Write the name of the person you are praying for on a card, and keep it where you pray these nine days.

days.title: Carried by Friends
days.verse: And they came, bringing to him a paralytic carried by four men. And when they could not get near him because of the crowd, they removed the roof above him; and when they had made an opening, they let down the pallet on which the paralytic lay.
days.refl: The paralyzed man could not reach Jesus on his own, so his friends carried him, and when the crowd blocked the way, they climbed up and opened the roof. Mark tells us that Jesus saw their faith. When someone we love is too tired or in too much pain to pray, our prayer can carry them. This novena is our stretcher: nine days of bringing them, together and with love, to the feet of the Lord who heals.
days.more: St. Camillus de Lellis knew what it meant to carry the sick. When the Tiber flooded Rome in 1598, he and his brothers went into the Hospital of the Holy Spirit and carried the patients to safety. Intercession is like that: we lend our strength to someone who has little left. No one needs to pray alone, and no sick person is ever forgotten by God.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, as four friends once carried a paralyzed man to You, we carry N. to You today. When they are too weary to pray, let our prayer be their stretcher, and let them feel the love of everyone who prays for them. Through the prayers of St. Camillus, who carried the sick in their need, keep us faithful in bringing N. to You every day.
days.step: Send N. or their family a short message, call or visit today, so they know N. is being prayed for.

days.title: Not Alone Through the Waters
days.verse: When you pass through the waters I will be with you; / and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; / when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, / and the flame shall not consume you.
days.refl: God does not promise that there will be no deep waters. He promises to be with us in them. A hospital corridor, a sleepless night, a long recovery, a diagnosis we did not want: these can feel like waters rising around us. Yet the Lord passes through them with us. In the Book of Tobit, God sent St. Raphael to walk beside young Tobias on a long and dangerous road, though Tobias did not yet know who his companion really was.
days.more: Tobias learned only at the end of the journey that his companion was an angel sent by God (Tobit 12). Often we, too, recognize God’s presence only when we look back. For now, it is enough to trust that Christ is with the sick in their pain and with all who love them. Even the last crossing is not made alone: Christ has passed through death and opened the way to eternal life.
days.prayer: Good Shepherd, walk with N. through these deep waters. When the road is long and the way ahead is unclear, let them sense that You are near. As St. Raphael guided Tobias on his journey, send Your holy angels to guard N. and all who care for them. Drive away our fear and fill our hearts with quiet trust in You.
days.step: Read Isaiah 43:1–3 slowly today, for N. or with them, and rest for a moment on the words “I will be with you.”

days.title: Asking Boldly for Healing
days.verse: And a leper came to him beseeching him, and kneeling said to him, “If you will, you can make me clean.” Moved with pity, he stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I will; be clean.”
days.refl: The leper kneels and asks plainly, with confidence and humility together: “If you will, you can.” Jesus is moved with pity, and He touches the man no one else would touch. We, too, may ask boldly for healing. God wants us to bring Him the desires of our hearts. So today we ask, without holding back, that the one we love be healed in body, and we leave the “if you will” in His loving hands.
days.more: At Lourdes in 1858, Our Lady told St. Bernadette to drink at the spring and wash there; she scraped the muddy ground and a spring began to flow. Some pilgrims have been cured there; many more have gone home with peace. If healing does not come, it is never a sign of weak faith: St. Paul begged three times to be freed of his affliction, and was answered with grace (2 Corinthians 12:8–9).
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You were moved with pity and stretched out Your hand to heal. We ask You boldly: if it is Your will, heal N. of this illness and restore their health. Bless every treatment and every medicine they receive. With Our Lady of Lourdes, Health of the Sick, and St. Bernadette praying for us, we place our request in Your hands with confidence and love.
days.step: Ask your parish, a prayer group or your family to remember N. in their prayers this week, or have a Mass offered for N.

days.title: Skill for Doctors & Nurses
days.verse: There is a time when success lies in the hands of physicians, for they too will pray to the Lord that he should grant them success in diagnosis and in healing, for the sake of preserving life.
days.refl: Sirach honors physicians as servants of the Lord, and reminds us that they, too, need prayer. God often heals through ordinary means: an accurate diagnosis, the right medicine, a careful surgeon, a nurse who notices a change in the night. Faith and medicine are not rivals. When we pray for the doctors and nurses who care for the one we love, we join our prayer to their skill and ask God to guide their minds and hands.
days.more: In the Book of Tobit, St. Raphael did not heal with a word alone. He told Tobias to keep the gall of a fish, and when Tobias put it on his father’s eyes, Tobit’s sight returned (Tobit 11). God used a remedy, a son’s care and an angel’s guidance together. This is one reason St. Raphael has long been invoked for physicians and for all who work for healing.
days.prayer: Lord, Giver of life, we pray for the doctors, nurses and all who care for N. Give them wisdom in diagnosis, skill in treatment, and gentleness in every word and touch. Through the prayers of St. Raphael, companion of Tobias, and St. Camillus, patron of nurses and hospitals, guide their decisions, protect them from tiredness and mistakes, and make their work an instrument of Your healing for N. and for all the sick.
days.step: Pray by name for one doctor, nurse or health worker caring for N., and thank someone in health care this week.

days.title: Strength for Caregivers
days.verse: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
days.refl: Illness is never carried by one person alone. Around every sick person there are others: a spouse at the bedside, parents or children rearranging their days, friends who drive, cook and sit through long waits. St. Paul says that bearing one another’s burdens is how we live the law of Christ. Caregiving is holy work, often hidden and tiring. Today we pray for everyone who looks after the one we love, and ask God to strengthen them.
days.more: St. Camillus asked his brothers to care for each sick person with the tenderness of a mother caring for her only sick child. He served the sick for decades while in pain himself, so he knew how tiring that love can be. Caregivers need care too: rest, food, someone to talk to, and time to pray. Accepting help is not weakness, and a tired caregiver’s quiet faithfulness is itself a prayer God sees.
days.prayer: Loving Father, bless all who care for N.: those at the bedside, those who cook and drive and wait, and those who pray from far away. Renew their strength when they are tired, their patience when they are stretched, and their hope when they are discouraged. Through the prayers of St. Camillus, servant of the sick, help us bear this burden together in love.
days.step: Offer a caregiver one practical help today: a meal, an errand, or an hour so they can rest.

days.title: Christ Carries Our Weakness
days.verse: This was to fulfil what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah, “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”
days.refl: Jesus did not keep His distance from human suffering. He touched the sick, and on the Cross He took our pain into Himself. No sickness is outside His reach, and no sick person suffers alone. Those who are ill can join their pain to His and offer it with love for others. This does not make suffering good in itself, but in Christ it is never wasted. It can become a prayer, even on days when words will not come.
days.more: St. Bernadette was not cured of her own illnesses. When she could no longer work, she said that her work now was to be sick, and she offered her sufferings for sinners. On the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes in 1984, Pope St. John Paul II taught that suffering joined to Christ shares in His work of redemption (Salvifici Doloris). We may pray for healing and offer our pain at the same time.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You took our infirmities and bore our diseases. Stay close to N. in every moment of pain, especially in long nights and anxious waiting, and give them the grace to join their suffering to Yours. Through the prayers of St. Bernadette, who offered her illness with love, give N. courage and peace. We trust that nothing they endure is wasted in Your loving hands.
days.step: Pause before a crucifix today, and offer Jesus one pain or worry of your own for N.

days.title: Healing of Heart & Spirit
days.verse: He heals the brokenhearted, / and binds up their wounds.
days.refl: Some wounds do not show on a scan: fear, discouragement, anger, the loneliness of a long illness, the strain it puts on a family. The Lord who heals bodies also binds up hearts. Today we ask for that deeper healing, for the one we love and for ourselves. Healing of the spirit may come before healing of the body, or alongside it, or as His gift even when the body does not recover. God’s care reaches every part of us.
days.more: The greatest healing in St. Camillus’s life happened inside. A soldier with a quick temper and a gambling habit, he was converted in 1575 and gave the rest of his life to God and the sick. The wound in his leg troubled him until he died, yet his heart was made new. The Church offers us this healing too, above all in Confession and in the Anointing of the Sick.
days.prayer: Lord, You heal the brokenhearted and bind up their wounds. Heal N. in spirit as well as in body: free them from fear and discouragement, and fill them with Your peace. Heal our hearts, too, of worry, impatience and anything that divides us, and make our home a place of peace. Through the prayers of St. Camillus, whose heart You made new, make us whole in You.
days.step: If you can, go to Confession this week, and gently ask N. or their family whether they would like a priest to bring Communion or the Anointing of the Sick.

days.title: Gratitude & Trust in God’s Will
days.verse: We know that in everything God works for good with those who love him, who are called according to his purpose.
days.refl: St. Paul does not say that everything that happens is good. He says that God is at work for good in everything, even in illness. We end these nine days not by demanding an outcome, but by giving thanks, because God has heard every prayer and answers in the way that is truly best. With Our Lady of Lourdes, St. Raphael, St. Camillus and St. Bernadette, we place the one we love in the hands of a faithful Father.
days.more: Looking back over these nine days, we may notice small graces: a good night’s sleep, a kind nurse, a clearer diagnosis, a calmer heart, a family drawn closer. Before St. Raphael told Tobit and Tobias who he was, he urged them to praise God and give thanks for all He had done (Tobit 12:6). Trusting God’s will does not mean we stop praying for healing; it means we keep praying in peace.
days.prayer: Lord, on this ninth day we thank You for Your faithfulness and for every grace, seen and unseen, that You have given N. and all of us. Thank you, Our Lady of Lourdes, St. Raphael, St. Camillus and St. Bernadette, for carrying our prayers before Jesus. We entrust N.’s health, their healing and their whole life to Your loving will, trusting that You will give what is truly good for N. and for us.
days.step: Write down three graces you noticed during these nine days, and thank God for them together.

printClosing: Beloved, I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in health;
I know that it is well with your soul.
